In-Person/VRI interpretation for Spoken Languages Services
notices.description: The Immigrant Services and Language Affairs (ISLA) division of The NYC Administration for Childrens Services (ACS) is seeking three vendors to provide In-Person/VRI interpretation for Spoken Languages, Deaf/Hard-of-Hearing Interpretation and Language services, and Written Translation Services. This Procurement will assist ACS compliance with Local Law 73 (2003), Local Law 30 (2017), the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II, and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which require ACS and its network of providers to provide interpretation and translation services for all limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families to enable equal access to ACS services, as well as ensure best practice for casework with limited-English proficient and deaf/hard of hearing families. The term of each of the contracts will be July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2029.

notices.short_title: Teen RAPP and Early RAPP Program Citywide
notices.description: The City of New York has a longstanding and on-going commitment to the prevention of dating violence and the building of healthy relationships and communities. This includes funding the Teen Relationship Abuse Prevention Program (Teen RAPP), which operates in approximately 40 middle and high schools throughout New York City, and the Early Relationship Abuse Prevention Program (E-RAPP), which operates in approximately 100 middle schools throughout the City. Teen RAPP places social workers from contracted community-based providers in schools to deliver a comprehensive array of teen dating violence services including prevention education, intervention counseling, staff development, and community outreach. E-RAPP offers classroom workshops, professional development for school staff and administration and training for parents.  The City's Relationship Abuse Prevention Program (RAPP), which serves both middle school and high school students, will be administered by the Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV) in partnership with the New York City Department of…

notices.agency_name: Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration
notices.short_title: Respect and Responsibility Services Program
notices.description: Respect and Responsibility is a key component of a larger Interrupting Violence at Home initiative, which was launched in 2018 and focuses on addressing intergenerational cycles of abuse through non-mandated community-based programming for people who cause harm. It is one of the first programs of its kind in the country and reflects the culmination of years of work led by ENDGBV, with City agencies, survivors, experts, and advocates and its partner agencies to develop new pathways to hold harm doers accountable. Working with people who cause harm is a critical component in New York City efforts to interrupt intimate partner violence, support survivors, and foster equitable, peaceful, and  A central part of this Initiative is the non-mandated, community-based programming for people causing harm in their relationships the Respect and Responsibility program. Respect and Responsibility will be administered by the Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV) in partnership with the New York City Department of Social Services/Human Resources Administration (DSS/HRA). This includes the 25% Allowance. Competition (1) Bronx and Manhattan.

notices.short_title: Advisory Services Regarding Co-Digestion and Renewable Natural Gas at Hunts Point Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility
notices.description:
The New York City Water Board (the Board) is issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) to solicit proposals from firms for purposes of providing advisory services to the Board and the New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) in connection with activities contemplated at DEPs Hunts Point Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility (Hunts Point WRRF), including the design and procurement of assets related to the co-digestion of waste materials, obtaining commercially viable natural gas from the biogas obtained from those wastewater materials, and the transport of natural gas to commercial purchasers.

The selected advisor or advisor(s) will support the Board and DEP across all phases of developing, structuring, and procuring a co-digestion and renewable natural gas program at the Hunts Point wastewater resource recovery facility.  The scope of work is expected to include evaluations drawn from disciplines which include engineering, finance, legal, tax planning, project management, procurement and supply ch…

notices.short_title: Expanding Access to a Nurse Care Manager Model
notices.vendor_name: William F. Ryan Community Health Center Inc
notices.description: Within the Health Department, the Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) is dedicated to reducing the morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. In accordance with this mission, this RFP aims to identify up to eight (8) safety-net primary care Contractors to develop and maintain their capacity to comprehensively identify and address the holistic health needs of people who use drugs (PWUD) and reduce substance use-related harms. This will be accomplished through the utilization of a nurse care manager-led collaborative care approach with the integration of low-barrier, medication-first, patient-centered, and harm reduction principles and approaches to engagement in care.

notices.short_title: July 21, 2026, Public Hearing Agenda
Notice of Adopted Final Report
notices.description:
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the New York City Charter Revision Commission appointed in December 2025 has issued its Adopted Final Report, dated June 25, 2026. The Adopted Final Report is available for public review at: https://dechert.box.com/s/sk211wqnr9em96mi7mwpwwnjmy4ddsyu.

NOTICE IS FURTHER GIVEN that the Commissions ballot proposal to establish non-partisan local elections with open primaries was unanimously approved by the Commission for placement on the November 2026 General Election ballot. The ballot proposal was transmitted to the New York City Clerk on May 27, 2026, and, following the Commissions adoption of a revised and corrected amendment, was retransmitted on June 25, 2026. The ballot proposal and amended submission are available for public review at: https://dechert.box.com/s/qwga6ahtb8yzj3mpkh2mqkt6jo657ii9.
